name: West End
tagline: One street, and every dive shop on it
description: A single sand-and-concrete street along the water at the island's western end, lined with dive shops, restaurants and bars, where almost every visitor and long-stay diver on Roatan ends up. It is walkable end to end in fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Divers and anyone who wants a community they can walk into
pros: Every dive operator on the island is here
The community is easy to join
Half Moon Bay for shore entry
cons: Busy when cruise ships are in
Internet is the weakest when the village fills

name: West Bay
tagline: The postcard beach, ten minutes further
description: The wide white beach around the western point from West End, with the reef close enough to swim to and the island's resorts along it. It is considerably more developed and more expensive than West End and rather less of a community.
bestFor: Anyone whose priority is the best beach on the island
pros: Reef snorkelling straight off the sand
Water taxi to West End in ten minutes
cons: The most expensive area on the island

name: Sandy Bay
tagline: Between the two, quieter and cheaper
description: A stretch of coast between West End and Coxen Hole, with the Roatan Institute for Marine Sciences, the botanical gardens and a scattering of houses and small hotels. It is where a lot of longer-term residents live, away from the visitor strip.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting local prices near the dive scene
pros: Cheaper than West End and West Bay
Ten minutes to West End by taxi

name: Coxen Hole
tagline: The working capital, with the ferry and the airport
description: Roatan's administrative town, holding the ferry terminal, the banks, the immigration office and the main supermarkets, with the airport just east of it. Visitors pass through rather than stay, but everything practical happens here.
bestFor: Anyone who needs banks, immigration or the ferry
pros: Ferry to La Ceiba and the airport
Cheapest food and shopping on the island
cons: Not a place to stay by choice

name: East End and Oak Ridge
tagline: The other half of the island, largely undeveloped
description: The long eastern arm of Roatan, with Oak Ridge's houses built out over the water, mangrove channels you can take a boat through, and Camp Bay's empty beach at the far end. Development thins out quickly past Punta Gorda.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the island without the visitor economy
pros: Oak Ridge's stilt houses and mangrove channels
The cheapest land and rent on Roatan
cons: Forty minutes or more from West End
Very limited services and weaker internet
